themes_detail.label: Garbage collection crisis escalating
themes_detail.summary: Missed Collection complaints spiked to 10 THIS WEEK versus a 1.8 weekly average over the prior 8 weeks—a 471% increase (z-score: 3.92)—signaling a potential breakdown in sanitation services in Brownsville/Ocean Hill.
evidence: 10 Missed Collection complaints THIS WEEK vs. 1.8 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (z-score: 3.92)
471% spike represents sharpest single-issue acceleration in district data
Complaints are current and ongoing; not historical pattern
reporting_angles: Interview affected residents about uncollected garbage piling up; tie to broader sanitation failures in under-resourced neighborhoods
Contact Sanitation Department for explanation of service disruption; ask if staffing or equipment shortages are responsible

themes_detail.label: Dead and dying trees surge
themes_detail.summary: Dead/Dying Tree complaints jumped to 3 THIS WEEK from a 0.6 weekly baseline over 8 weeks—a 380% spike (z-score: 3.41)—suggesting environmental neglect or disease outbreak in the district's street tree canopy.
evidence: 3 Dead/Dying Tree complaints THIS WEEK vs. 0.6 weekly average (z-score: 3.41, 380% increase)
Baseline is historically very low (0.6/week), making even small absolute numbers statistically significant
May indicate either seasonal disease cycle, lack of maintenance, or weather stress
reporting_angles: Walk affected blocks and photograph dead/dying trees; identify which species and neighborhoods hardest hit
Interview Parks Department about tree maintenance budget and disease monitoring in Brownsville; compare to other districts

themes_detail.label: Sewer system distress signals
themes_detail.summary: Sewer complaints spiked to 19 THREE WEEKS AGO versus a 5.9 weekly average—a 223% increase (z-score: 4.61)—but this is the oldest signal in current dataset; verify whether issue has persisted into this week before pursuing.
evidence: 19 Sewer complaints 3 weeks ago vs. 5.9 weekly average (z-score: 4.61, 223% spike)
Related: Root/Sewer/Sidewalk Condition complaints at 4 (2 weeks ago) vs. 1.1 baseline (256% increase, z-score: 3.1)
Sewer spike predates current week; unclear if resolved or ongoing—requires verification
reporting_angles: Check 311 data for this week to confirm whether sewer complaints have subsided or persisted; interview DEP about known issues
Investigate whether sewer problems are connected to sidewalk deterioration and root damage; examine maintenance records

themes_detail.label: Cannabis retail complaints double
themes_detail.summary: Cannabis Retailer complaints jumped to 7 TWO WEEKS AGO versus a 2.0 weekly average—a 250% spike (z-score: 4.47)—suggesting community friction over unlicensed or non-compliant shops in Brownsville/Ocean Hill.
evidence: 7 Cannabis Retailer complaints 2 weeks ago vs. 2.0 weekly average (z-score: 4.47, 250% increase)
Small absolute volume (7 complaints) but statistically anomalous given low baseline
Pattern suggests either enforcement crackdown, new retail openings, or resident complaints about operations (odor, foot traffic, etc.)
reporting_angles: Map recent cannabis retail license approvals and denials in the district; interview Community Board about enforcement concerns
Interview residents and business owners about complaints (illegal shops, odor, loitering); assess overlap with licensed vs. unlicensed storefronts

themes_detail.label: Sidewalk deterioration accelerating
themes_detail.summary: Sidewalk Condition complaints hit 7 THREE WEEKS AGO versus a 2.2 weekly average—a 211% spike (z-score: 3.66)—indicating growing pedestrian safety hazards, though this signal is 3 weeks old and needs current-week confirmation.
evidence: 7 Sidewalk Condition complaints 3 weeks ago vs. 2.2 weekly average (z-score: 3.66, 211% increase)
Converges with Root/Sewer/Sidewalk complaints spike 2 weeks ago (4 vs. 1.1 baseline), suggesting infrastructure-wide degradation
Signal is 3 weeks old; recency is lower than garbage and tree spikes—requires verification of current status
reporting_angles: Audit sidewalk conditions on main commercial corridors (Nostrand Ave, Fulton St, Atlantic Ave); photograph tripping hazards and broken pavement
Interview DOT about maintenance backlog and budget constraints; cross-reference with DOB permit filings (398 alterations filed—are property owners maintaining sidewalks?)
